neighbours.label: Completes non-physio words with -ology, -ological, -ologist, or -ologists, including biological.
fire: During registration, Maya chose biology as her optional course for the spring term.
The report described biological changes in seedlings after three weeks of reduced sunlight.
At the museum, we found a geology textbook beneath a stack of old maps.
Before construction began, the team requested a geological assessment of the proposed tunnel route.
After the interview, the sociologist compared family routines across several nearby apartment buildings.
Outside the village, archaeologists uncovered a stone doorway beneath layers of windblown sand.
In her notebook, Lina wrote dragonology as the invented name for studying imaginary dragons.
During review, the editor questioned the methodological assumptions underlying the comparison between the two groups.
quiet: For her optional course, Maya selected the study of living organisms during spring registration.
Researchers documented biochemical changes in young seedlings exposed to several weeks of reduced sunlight.
Beneath some old maps lay a textbook about rocks and the structure of Earth.
The proposed tunnel required an assessment of local rock formations before construction could begin.
After lunch, the physiologist compared breathing patterns across several groups of healthy adult volunteers.
Near the village boundary, excavators discovered a stone doorway buried under windblown sand.
On a notebook page, Lina invented dragoncraft as a name for studying imaginary dragons.
A reviewer challenged the experimental assumptions behind the comparison between the two groups.
